output.reason: The closed FCSTM has a fundamentally split topology: the root's real initial edge (transition:line:21, sourced from tr_0001/@initial:__root__ -> InitialState) enters only InitialState, a leaf with no outgoing transition, while Region1 and Region2 (and everything inside them, including TargetSearch/FormationAdjustment/AttackReady/Attack and all four events) are structurally disconnected from that initial entry. Deterministic inspection-equivalent and verify facts confirm: reachable_state_refs={root, InitialState}; Region1/Region2 and their children are STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL and reachability-refuted; all four events are EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE/event-consumer-refuted; InitialState itself is LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-refuted. This drives behavior-consequence candidates: (1) the NL2 state_action progress obligation over the UAV search operation is a dead end because the only reachable state has zero outgoing transitions and the search-region states are unreachable; (2) NL3 and NL4 event-consumer coverage obligations show declared-but-unreachable consumers, which is the reachable-consumer coverage failure; (3) I derive one composite reachability obligation because Region1 and Region2 jointly constitute the search operation's state areas but neither composite has any root-owned entry, which is a distinct owner/root reachability defect from the local child initial edges (tr_0002, tr_0005) that only work once their region is entered. Cardinality binding: NL2's 'three different state areas' can plausibly be read as three top-level siblings (InitialState, Region1, Region2) or as concurrent regions given the explicit PlantUML '--' separators; I record this as ambiguous per protocol since no exact single primary domain is established by NL alone.

issues.reason: NL2 requires the search operation to continuously perform tasks (progress obligation) before mission completion; the closed model's only reachable state is a deadlock leaf and the states that would carry search activity are unreachable, which is exactly the reachable nonterminal-no-progress/frontier fact V1 is meant to certify.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The child-scoped initial edges tr_0002 (@initial:Region1->TargetSearch) and tr_0005 (@initial:Region2->AttackReady) exist and would let search activity progress once their region is entered; the defect is entry into Region1/Region2 from root, not absence of local continuation logic within those regions.
issues.title: Search operation cannot progress: only reachable state is a zero-outgoing leaf, search regions unreachable

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for Interception_Detected (reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Interception_Detected; verify_facts check event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted.
issues.expected: The interception event must be accepted by a reachable consumer transition within the UAV swarm's search operation scope whenever it occurs.
issues.observed: event_consumers shows Interception_Detected has declared consumer transition:line:10 (TargetSearch->FormationAdjustment) but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_state_refs=[]; diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE confirms consumers exist but none is reachable from a top-level initial entry; verify_facts event-consumer check status=refuted.
issues.reason: The event_consumer_coverage property requires a reachable consumer, not merely a declared one; the deterministic facts show declaration-only presence, which is the exact operational-coverage gap this contract targets and for which no frozen predicate directly certifies reachable event consumption, so it remains a precise predicate-null W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition itself is structurally present and correctly wired inside Region1, so if root-level entry into Region1 were repaired the event would become consumable without further edits to this transition.
issues.title: Interception event has a declared consumer transition but no reachable consumer from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for Task_Assignment_Received (reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Task_Assignment_Received; verify_facts check event-consumer:Task_Assignment_Received status=refuted.
issues.expected: The task-assignment-received event must be accepted by a reachable consumer transition in the UAV swarm's in-flight operation scope whenever it occurs.
issues.observed: event_consumers shows Task_Assignment_Received has declared consumer transition:line:17 (AttackReady->Attack) but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_state_refs=[]; diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE confirms this; verify_facts event-consumer check status=refuted because Region2 and its children are unreachable from root.
issues.reason: Reachable operational coverage of the task-assignment event fails even though a consumer transition is declared; declaration alone does not discharge the stronger reachable-consumer property required by this contract, and no frozen predicate expresses reachable event-consumer coverage, so this remains a precise predicate-null W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition AttackReady->Attack is correctly authored and would become consumable if Region2 gained a root-level entry; the transition's own trigger/target wiring is not itself defective.
issues.title: Task-assignment event has a declared consumer transition but no reachable consumer from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts states Region1/Region2 reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts reachability checks for state:Region1:line:6 and state:Region2:line:13 status=refuted; fcstm_model shows root's sole outgoing transition (line:21) targets InitialState only, never Region1/Region2; NL2 quote establishing the three state areas as the search operation's structure.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm's search-operation scope (its constituent composite regions/state areas) must be reachable from the root of the closed model so that the described continuous behavior can actually execute.
issues.observed: Region1 and Region2 (state:Region1:line:6, state:Region2:line:13), the two composites that carry all search/attack behavior, are marked STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL and reachability-refuted by verify_facts; only the root wrapper and the disconnected InitialState leaf are reachable_from_initial=true. The root's only outgoing edge (transition:line:21) targets InitialState, not Region1 or Region2, so the entire search-operation scope the NL describes is topologically isolated from the closed model's actual initial entry.
issues.reason: NL2 establishes that the UAV swarm's search operation is organized as concurrent state areas that must continuously execute; cross-view grounding reveals this is not a mere state_action progress gap on one state but a structural root-reachability failure of the entire owning composite scope (Region1/Region2), which is a distinct frontier property from the local per-region initial-entry edges (tr_0002/tr_0005) that already exist inside each region. This derived reachability obligation isolates that exact global defect for G1 finite path-existence assessment (root to Region1 has no path).
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each region does have its own local initial pseudostate edge (tr_0002 into TargetSearch, tr_0005 into AttackReady), so once entered, each region's internal continuation logic is intact; the defect is confined to the missing root-to-region entry rather than any malformed regional logic.
issues.title: The two composite regions that realize the UAV swarm's search operation are unreachable from root, isolating the entire operational scope

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive/title context and contains no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes both a cardinality/region obligation (three state areas) and a continuous state_action obligation (continuously performs target search) scoped before mission completion, plus an implicit termination context (mission completed) that is too vague to bind as a distinct termination contract without a named terminal state, so it is preserved only as scope context in the state_action/cardinality contracts. NL3 establishes an interception-triggered transition to a formation-adjustment state; source is the enclosing continuing operating scope (the UAV swarm's ongoing search operation) captured via the resolved 'UAV swarm' operating context, target is FormationAdjustment. NL4 establishes a task-assignment-triggered transition into Attack state and a decrease-in-UAV-count effect that fires after completing the attack, treated as a variable_delta obligation on the UAV count variable scoped to the attack completion event.
